properties.description:
DECISION 4, built 2026-08-20 on Anthony's word. DISTINCT FROM the fact that measured the defect: that node is the MEASUREMENT and is now closed with valid_to; this is the REMEDY. Conflating them would leave the design unable to say whether the fix happened.

THE DEFECT, found by running the loop honestly rather than looking for it: epoch:the-declared-walls-hold was set arrived with BOTH its capabilities genuinely delivered, and arrival_delta reported both `outstanding`. Delivery required an Artifact on disk; model work produces none. `outstanding` means "nobody has said whether this was deferred or discontinued - that is the question to put to the user", so reflow2 asked a question about finished work and would ask it again every run. Re-decompositions, retirements, governance rulings and corrections all produce no file; every one would pile up as a phantom incompletion until somebody stopped scheduling that kind of work, which is most of what systems engineering is.

WHAT SHIPPED: Capability.delivery, an enum of `artifact` (default) or `model`, plus set_capability_delivery to declare it.
  · `artifact` - a file realizes it AND a check passes. Unchanged, and the case almost every capability is in.
  · `model` - the deliverable IS the design change, so the check is the whole of the evidence.

⭐ IT DECLARES THE KIND, NEVER THE SUCCESS, and that is the whole reason it is safe to let an author state it. Both kinds still demand a passing check: the declaration loosens WHICH evidence is required, never WHETHER any is. Delivery stays computed from the golden thread, there is still no `achieved` modality, and there is still no way to mark anything done. Same shape as Interface.designation and Artifact.volatility - the author says the one thing only they can know, the computation earns the rest.

🛑 THE REJECTED FIX, recorded because it was the version first proposed AND first approved, and it is wrong: inferring `model` from the ABSENCE of an artifact. The commonest reason a capability has no file is THAT NOBODY HAS BUILT IT YET. cap:graph-registry is in exactly that state today - unbuilt, unrealized - and under the inferred rule it would report DELIVERED the moment any check was pointed at it. A false green on unbuilt work, in the same dangerous direction as a detector reporting clean because it had nothing to run on. an_unbuilt_capability_with_a_passing_check_is_not_delivered pins it.

⭐ THE REMEDY IS REACHABLE FROM THE MESSAGE THE READER SEES. Fixing the rule alone would have left the declaration built, tested and invisible - the same failure found FOUR separate times on 2026-08-20. arrival_delta now names set_capability_delivery when it reports an outstanding item that HAS a passing check and nothing on disk, and stays silent when there is no check at all, because then declaring model would not help either and the suggestion would be noise. It also does not accuse: it ends by saying that if the work is simply unbuilt, `outstanding` is correct.

PROVEN ON THE CASE THAT FOUND IT, not only on fixtures: both capabilities of epoch:the-declared-walls-hold were declared `model` through the served tool against the live graph, and the increment went from two `outstanding` to two `delivered`.

STATED LIMIT, unchanged by this: an increment with nothing scheduled `required` is still reported as not ready to cut, while the plan-increments skill says `required` must be asked for and never assumed. A user following reflow2's own guidance still builds an increment reflow2 calls unscoped. That tension is recorded and NOT fixed here.
properties.name: A capability declares WHAT KIND of thing delivers it, so model work can be reported delivered
